_meta.note: Prototype knowledge base. Amounts, limits and links change often: verify on the official portal before applying.

schemes.name: Udyam Registration
schemes.desc: Free online registration that gives a business its official MSME identity. Unlocks priority-sector loans, credit guarantee cover and delayed-payment protection.
schemes.benefit: Udyam certificate and number; access to MSME schemes and the delayed-payment mechanism.
schemes.eligibility: Any micro, small or medium enterprise (manufacturing or services). Self-declaration, Aadhaar-linked.
docs: Aadhaar of proprietor / partner / authorised signatory (with mobile linked for OTP)
PAN (and GSTIN if you have one)
Business activity (NIC code), employee count, investment and turnover figures
steps: Open the Udyam Registration portal and choose 'New Entrepreneur'
Verify Aadhaar by OTP, then PAN
Enter business name, address, activity, employees, investment and turnover
Submit and download the certificate with your Udyam number. Registration is free

schemes.name: Certificate of Vending (Street Vendors Act, 2014)
schemes.desc: Legal recognition as a street vendor. The Act requires a survey, vending zones, notice and due process before relocation or eviction.
schemes.benefit: Vending certificate / ID card; right to vend in a designated zone; protection against arbitrary eviction.
schemes.eligibility: Street vendors enrolled in the Urban Local Body (municipality) survey, or applying to the Town Vending Committee.
docs: Proof of existing vending (photos, receipts, witness statement)
steps: Visit your ward office / municipality and ask for the street-vendor survey or enrolment
Submit identity proof and proof of vending
Collect the certificate or ID card and keep copies
If delayed, rejected or evicted without notice, complain to the Town Vending Committee and its grievance redressal committee

schemes.name: PM SVANidhi
schemes.desc: Collateral-free working-capital loans for street vendors, with incentives for digital payments and timely repayment.
schemes.benefit: Tiered working-capital loans (first tranche ₹15,000 under the restructured scheme; higher tranches on timely repayment). Confirm current limits on the portal.
schemes.eligibility: Urban street vendors with a Certificate of Vending / ID card, or a Letter of Recommendation from the Urban Local Body.
docs: Certificate of Vending / ID card, or ULB Letter of Recommendation
steps: Check your vendor survey / ID status with your Urban Local Body
If you have no certificate, request a Letter of Recommendation from the ULB / Town Vending Committee
Apply on the PM SVANidhi portal or through a Common Service Centre using Aadhaar eKYC
Accept the loan from the participating bank / NBFC / MFI and repay on time to unlock the next tranche

schemes.name: PM MUDRA Yojana
schemes.desc: Collateral-free loans for non-farm micro and small businesses in four bands: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishor (₹50,001 to ₹5 lakh), Tarun (₹5 to ₹10 lakh) and Tarun Plus (up to ₹20 lakh).
schemes.benefit: Loans up to ₹20 lakh without collateral for working capital or equipment.
schemes.eligibility: Non-farm, non-corporate income-generating businesses: trading, manufacturing, services, food, artisan work.
docs: Business proof (Udyam / licence / vending certificate where available)
Short business plan or quotation for equipment
steps: Pick the band that matches your need
Apply at a bank, NBFC or MFI, or through the Jan Samarth / MUDRA portal
Submit KYC and business proof
Track the application; no collateral is required for MUDRA loans

schemes.name: CGTMSE Credit Guarantee
schemes.desc: Government-backed guarantee so banks can lend to micro and small enterprises without collateral or third-party guarantee.
schemes.benefit: Collateral-free credit cover for eligible loans (cap is revised periodically; verify the current limit).
schemes.eligibility: New or existing micro and small enterprises borrowing from a participating lender. Udyam registration is usually expected.
steps: Register on Udyam
Ask the bank for a loan under CGTMSE cover
The lender applies for the guarantee; you do not file with CGTMSE yourself

schemes.name: PMEGP (subsidy-linked loan for new units)
schemes.desc: Margin-money subsidy on bank loans for setting up new micro enterprises in manufacturing or services.
schemes.benefit: Subsidy of roughly 15% to 35% of project cost depending on category and area; project cost ceiling ₹50 lakh (manufacturing) and ₹20 lakh (service).
schemes.eligibility: New units only; age 18+; 8th pass for larger projects. Not for units that already got a subsidy under another scheme.
docs: Caste / special-category certificate if claiming higher subsidy
steps: Prepare a project report
Apply on the PMEGP e-portal and select a bank
Attend the DIC / bank interview and training if asked
After loan sanction the subsidy is credited to the bank account as margin money

schemes.name: Stand-Up India
schemes.desc: Bank loans between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore for greenfield enterprises led by women or SC/ST entrepreneurs.
schemes.benefit: One loan per bank branch for first-time enterprises in manufacturing, services or trading.
schemes.eligibility: Women and/or SC/ST entrepreneurs, 18+, setting up a first (greenfield) enterprise.
steps: Prepare a project report
Apply through the Stand-Up Mitra portal or directly at a bank branch
Submit KYC and category certificate
Follow up with the lending branch

schemes.name: PM FME (micro food processing)
schemes.desc: Credit-linked subsidy for upgrading or formalising micro food-processing units.
schemes.benefit: 35% credit-linked subsidy on eligible project cost, capped at ₹10 lakh per unit.
schemes.eligibility: Existing individual micro food-processing units (pickle, papad, masala, bakery, flour, oil and similar).
docs: Detailed project report for the upgrade
steps: Contact the District Resource Person or State Nodal Agency
Prepare the project report for the upgrade
Apply on the PM FME portal
Bank sanctions the loan; subsidy is released against it

schemes.name: PM Vishwakarma
schemes.desc: Support for artisans and craftspeople in 18 traditional trades: recognition, skill training with stipend, toolkit incentive and low-interest credit.
schemes.benefit: PM Vishwakarma certificate and ID, training stipend, toolkit incentive of ₹15,000, collateral-free credit starting at ₹1 lakh at a concessional rate.
schemes.eligibility: Artisans in listed trades (carpenter, tailor, potter, blacksmith, goldsmith, cobbler, mason, barber, washerman, weaver and others), 18+.
steps: Register at a Common Service Centre or on the portal
Complete Aadhaar-based biometric verification
Verification by Gram Panchayat / ULB and district committee
Receive certificate, training and toolkit, then apply for credit

schemes.name: FSSAI Registration / Licence
schemes.desc: Mandatory food-business authorisation. Basic registration for small operators; a State or Central licence for larger turnover.
schemes.benefit: Legal permission to run a food business and display the FSSAI number on bills and premises.
schemes.eligibility: All food businesses. Registration is for turnover up to ₹12 lakh a year; a licence is needed above that or for certain categories.
docs: Food safety management plan and layout (licence only)
steps: Create an account on the FoSCoS portal
Choose Registration or Licence based on turnover and category
Upload documents and pay the fee
Inspection if required, then download the certificate

schemes.name: GST Registration
schemes.desc: Tax registration. Mandatory above the turnover threshold, for inter-state supply of goods and for e-commerce sellers.
schemes.benefit: Legal invoicing, input tax credit, ability to sell to larger buyers.
schemes.eligibility: Mandatory above ₹40 lakh turnover for goods and ₹20 lakh for services (lower in some special-category states); voluntary below that unless inter-state or e-commerce.
steps: File Part A on the GST portal with PAN, mobile and email
Complete Part B with business details and upload documents
Aadhaar authentication
Receive the ARN and then the GSTIN once approved

schemes.name: Trade / Municipal Licence
schemes.desc: Local licence to operate a shop, eatery or workshop in your municipal area. Rules and fees are set by your municipality, so confirm locally.
schemes.benefit: Legal premises operation; commonly asked for by banks and landlords.
schemes.eligibility: Shops, eateries, workshops and service premises within a municipal area.
docs: Proof of premises (rent agreement / ownership / NOC)
steps: Find your municipal corporation's trade-licence portal or licence department (for example KMC in Kolkata)
Submit the application with premises proof and fee
Inspection if required
Collect the licence and renew it before expiry

schemes.name: Shops & Establishments Registration
schemes.desc: State registration covering working hours, holidays and employee rules for shops, offices and commercial establishments.
schemes.benefit: State-law compliance for shops and establishments; commonly needed for bank accounts and licences.
schemes.eligibility: Shops and commercial establishments, with thresholds that vary by state.
steps: Open your state labour department portal
Fill the registration form with premises and employee details
Upload documents and pay the fee
Download the certificate

schemes.name: MSME Samadhaan (delayed payment)
schemes.desc: Online filing for delayed payments by buyers. Under the MSMED Act, 2006, buyers must pay within the agreed time (at most 45 days). Unpaid amounts carry compound interest at three times the RBI bank rate, with monthly rests.
schemes.benefit: Reference to the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council for conciliation and arbitration.
schemes.eligibility: Micro and small suppliers with Udyam registration owed money for goods or services.
steps: Send a written demand notice citing Sections 15 and 16 of the MSMED Act
If unpaid, file on the MSME Samadhaan portal with invoices and proof
Attend conciliation before the Facilitation Council (Section 18)
If conciliation fails, the Council arbitrates or refers to an institution for arbitration

schemes.name: CPGRAMS (public grievances)
schemes.desc: Central portal to lodge complaints against central and state government departments, with tracking and appeal.
schemes.benefit: Registered grievance with a tracking number and a defined redress timeline.
schemes.eligibility: Any citizen with a grievance about public service delivery.
docs: Details of the grievance and department
steps: Open the CPGRAMS portal and register
Select the ministry or department and describe the issue
Attach documents and submit
Track status and use the appeal option if unsatisfied

schemes.name: National Consumer Helpline / e-Daakhil
schemes.desc: Pre-litigation mediation through the helpline (1915) and online filing of consumer cases through e-Daakhil.
schemes.benefit: Refund / replacement / compensation route for defective goods, deficient services and unfair practices.
schemes.eligibility: Consumers who bought goods or services from a seller or provider.
steps: Call 1915 or register the complaint on the consumer helpline portal
Send the seller a written notice with a deadline
If unresolved, file a consumer complaint online through e-Daakhil in the right commission
Attend hearings or mediation
